THE DB PROBE ON A MISS of test (2) is `pg_isready -h "$sockdir" -p 5432 -q` (a real round trip, only paid when the socket file is absent — a socket file can outlive a crashed server, so the miss path re-asks with the real question); if it answers, the floor is up and nothing is started. If not, the start is ONE call, `sudo -n systemctl start postgresql.service` (measured: this box runs the debian cluster `postgresql@16-main.service`, started through the umbrella `postgresql.service`; there is NO start tooling in cairn/devices/db_domain — `grep -rn 'pg_ctl\|systemctl' cairn/devices/db_domain/*.py` is empty — so this call is the one place the db is started from, and the store's own connect() (store.py:90) then finds it). After a start that returned 0, poll THE SOCKET FILE (`[[ -S "$CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR/.s.PGSQL.5432" ]]`, the same path test (2) reads) — `sleep 0.2` between attempts, 75 attempts, 15s in all; the first hit returns 0. The 75th miss → `cairn: floor: db — postgres was started (systemctl start postgresql.service returned 0) but <socket> did not appear within 15s`, exit 3. A start that returned non-zero never reaches the poll: `cairn: floor: db — postgres is down at <socket> and this user could not start it (sudo -n systemctl start postgresql.service: <sudo's own words, or 'refused' if it said nothing>); lay the sudoers line once — the ollama line's twin, for /bin/systemctl start postgresql.service — or run: cairn sudorelay`, exit 3. `pg_isready` is asked exactly once, before the start, on the socket-file miss, and always on `-h "$CAIRN_PG_SOCKET_DIR" -p 5432` (the D3 variable, default /var/run/postgresql) — measured at cairn 09475560, bin/cairn:106-123 (`_floor_db`).
